cohort: The study involved 65 COVID-19 positive mothers undergoing a Caesarean section, comparing them with a group of COVID-19 negative mothers who also underwent Caesarean sections, and also comparing overall Caesarean section rates between COVID-19 affected and unaffected pregnancies.
finding: COVID-19-affected mothers had a higher caesarean section rate, and among those undergoing C-section, they showed increased prevalence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, anaemia requiring blood transfusion, and postoperative urinary tract infections compared to COVID-19 negative mothers.
mod_finding: COVID-19-affected women had a significantly higher caesarean section rate (44.5%) compared to non-affected women (32.8%).
birth_weight: Prevalence of low birth weight (30%) was reported in babies born to COVID-19 positive mothers undergoing C-section.
